## Conclusion 

Given my analysis, the correlation between students with little to no coding experience finding video lessons effective, is somewhat both inconclusive and supported. Given the plotted data on my visual chart #2, students with coding experience of 'None to less than one month', '7-12 months', and '1-2 years' all rated video lesson effectiveness with a score between 4-7 out of 7. This data does not support that only students with specifically the least amount of coding experience feel video lessons are effective. But rather, the data does show that most coding students with various backgrounds of experience find video lessons effective. Additionally, I feel that experimental data that recorded the performance on quizzes of students who watched video lessons versus students who didn't watch video lessons could objectively conclude their effectiveness. If my course improvement idea to require video lessons to be watched was implemented, I feel it would potentially help many coding students who find it affective, however, it would negatively affect students who don't find video lessons affective because it would consume more of their time on a study method they don't feel is affective.
